summary: Repaired /srv/legacy2/stale-pidfile-startup/bin/control. The worker is healthy after a verified node reboot, with PID 1634. The original journal entry, RHEL release, and kernel were preserved.
actions_performed: Added process-identity validation instead of trusting PID-file existence.
Added distinct live, stale, foreign-process, and stopped states.
Added serialized start/stop operations and atomic PID-file updates.
Made repeated starts reuse or adopt the existing worker.
Made stop avoid signalling stale or unrelated PIDs.
Tested stale-PID recovery, repeated starts, foreign-PID handling, safe stopping, journal preservation, and reboot persistence.

evidence.requirement: Distinguish and recover from a stale PID
evidence.summary: After an unclean stop, PID 2798 remained in the file, status returned stale/1, and start removed it and launched a healthy worker.

evidence.requirement: Distinguish a PID belonging to another process and leave it running
evidence.summary: Status returned foreign-process/2. Start and stop left the unrelated process alive; no unrelated PID was signalled.

evidence.requirement: Repeated starts retain exactly one worker
evidence.summary: Repeated starts retained the same PID, and direct process scans found exactly one worker.

evidence.requirement: Stopping removes the worker without affecting unrelated processes
evidence.summary: The worker was absent after stop while the unrelated test process remained alive.
The original 'previous worker completed batch B100' record remained the first line before and after repair and reboot; new ticks were appended.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel

evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline under boot f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c, received reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot c8a39725-1d97-4329-aed3-aabe596a685e, then recovered through the retained stale PID file. Post-restart proof shows one live worker, preserved journal data, and the unchanged control-script hash.
